claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First of all, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Yes, I'm looking to claim Child Benefit. I have one child - my son Alex, who's 19 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information!

Since Alex is 19 years old, he's over 16, so I need to ask a few more questions to determine your eligibility.

Is Alex currently in approved education or training? This would include things like:
- A-levels or equivalent
- Scottish Highers
- NVQs up to level 3
- A course that prepares them for an apprenticeship or employment

(Note: Apprenticeships in England, paid work of 24 hours or more per week, or higher education like university degrees do not count as approved education or training for Child Benefit purposes.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is still in education. He's studying for his A-levels at the local sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great, thank you for confirming that Alex is studying for his A-levels at sixth form college. A-levels count as approved education, which is positive for your eligibility.

Now, I have a few more questions:

Do you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! That's helpful to know.

Next, could you confirm your living situation with Alex? Does Alex live with you, or does he live elsewhere?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for confirming that.

Just a couple more questions:

1. Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?
2. Does Alex work 24 hours or more per week, or receive any benefits in his own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. And no, he doesn't work - he's focused on his A-levels. He doesn't receive any benefits in his own name either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. I now have everything I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:

- You live in the UK (Manchester)
- Alex is 19 years old and lives with you
- He is in approved education (studying A-levels at sixth form college)
- He does not work 24 hours or more per week
- He does not receive benefits in his own right
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

Let me now provide you with my assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why:

**For Alex (age 19):**
- ✅ You live in the UK
- ✅ Alex lives with you, so you are responsible for him
- ✅ Although Alex is over 16, he is under 20 and is in approved education (A-levels count as approved education)
- ✅ No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- ✅ Alex does not work 24 hours or more per week
- ✅ Alex does not receive benefits in his own right

You can make a claim for Child Benefit through the government's official channels. Please note that you'll need to inform HMRC if Alex's circumstances change, such as if he finishes his A-levels, starts working 24+ hours per week, or begins receiving benefits.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
